Implementation synthesis: use `model.eval()` and `torch.inference_mode()`, freeze each user’s appended-MASK feature, and score ascending catalog-ID chunks through the trained scoring head, including any bias/transformation. Exclude PAD, MASK and every item in the complete observed prefix, including interactions truncated from the encoder input. Require an eligible target. Check raw scores with `torch.isfinite` before exclusions; reject NaN/Inf instead of repairing them. Filter excluded entries before selection so sentinels cannot enter short recommendation lists. [Finite checks](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.isfinite.html).

Define order as descending score, then ascending item ID. Sort IDs ascending before `argsort(scores, descending=True, stable=True)`; plain `topk` cannot guarantee tie membership. Stream top-11 by merging retained entries with each chunk’s eligible top-11 using that same order. Obtain the target score from its canonical catalog chunk; a second identical scoring pass can accumulate `rank = 1 + count((score > target_score) | ((score == target_score) & (id < target_id)))` over eligible items. Gather sampled-candidate scores during catalog traversal and reuse them, including the target score. With unique sampled candidates drawn from the same eligible universe, sampled rank must not exceed catalog rank. [Stable sorting](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.argsort.html), [topk limitations](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.topk.html).

“Exact” means exhaustive ranking of the computed scores. PyTorch does not guarantee bitwise equality between batched and sliced matrix multiplications; changed user batches or catalog chunks can change kernels, rounding and near-tie order. Pin batch/chunk shapes, dtype, precision settings, software and hardware; preserve shapes across repeated passes. Reusing catalog scores prevents separately computed candidate scores from invalidating nested-rank checks. Avoid epsilon tie rules. [Numerical accuracy](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/main/notes/numerical_accuracy.html).
